questions.text: RepairTrack is a repair booking system. A Client registers a Device and creates a RepairRequest describing a fault. A Technician is assigned to requests and records inspections, quoted cost and repair status. The Client accepts or rejects a quote. Accepted jobs are repaired and closed; rejected jobs are returned unmodified. Each RepairRequest belongs to one Client and one Device. A Client can have several requests; one Technician can handle several requests. Write a fully developed use case description for 'Approve repair quote'. Include primary actor, trigger, preconditions, main success steps, at least two alternate paths and postconditions.
questions.correctAnswer: Name: Approve repair quote. Actor: Client. Trigger: quote available. Preconditions: Client authenticated; quote applies to a pending RepairRequest. Main: Client opens request; system shows cost and scope; Client accepts; system verifies quote current, records decision and notifies Technician; request moves to approved. Alternatives: reject quote -> rejected state/return device; quote expired -> request new quotation; permission failure -> deny update. Postconditions: accurate quote decision and next step recorded.

questions.text: Write simple language-neutral pseudocode for a function called canApproveQuote. It receives an authenticatedClientId and a repairRequest. It must return false if the request does not belong to this client, the quote is missing or the quote has expired; otherwise it returns true only if the request status is 'Quoted'. Explain why the checks are ordered safely.
questions.correctAnswer:
function canApproveQuote(clientId, request):
    if request is null: return false
    if request.clientId != clientId: return false
    if request.quote is null: return false
    if request.quote.expiresAt < now(): return false
    return request.status == 'Quoted'
aiRubric: Defines function accepting caller and request
Explains safe access order / equivalent logic
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Pseudocode states intended logic without relying on one exact programming-language syntax. Check that objects exist before reading their fields. Validate ownership and business conditions. Return true only when all required conditions pass. Equivalent safe pseudocode earns credit. The app reviews the solution against a rubric; it does not execute submitted code.
questions.explanation:

1. Check that objects exist before reading their fields.
